REVIEW TEXT Ordered 2 dinners to go. They do not provide silverwear even when specifically asked for some. I mean cant be to hard to buy some silverwear at the dokkar store so u could provide to customers who spend about 20 a piece on dinner. I find it lazy, and cheap. This is not the first time weve came into town to grab dinner and leave with no utensils to  eat it with.   Ridiculous.
The chicken tortillini salad is a favorite of many ppls around here however they seperate it into a few diff things so u need to mix it yourself. I dont know how much of this stuff to pour on the salad to make it taste normal.  Could it not just be mixed before hand? So u only have to add 1 thing ontop of the lettuce? If these things were fixed prob 5 star. A bit high price , but id still consider it.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT The ordering experience was an adventure. Order food one side order beer the other find a place to sit. The poutine's fries were very salty, I thought it was the gravy at first but checked my wife's fries and they were very salty as well.  The brisket was good, tender and nice flavor i pick all that out.  The extra cheese was a big glob on the bottom of the fries so that was a loss.  The brisket dip was good but had quite a bit of untrimmed fat attached. It came with a dip that was a thinned out bbq sauce. I was expecting more of a savory than sweet dip.  My wife's black and blue was described as not enough blue cheese or just not as strong a blue cheese flavor as she expected.

REVIEW TEXT Good atmosphere. Good beer. The food was good too. I bet it would be even better if it were served fresh. That’s where the two stars come from otherwise it would be a 1.
HOWEVER, when we went to order, the clerk wasn’t at the register. She asked my husband the order anyways and immediately forgot what he’d said. We waited over 30+ minutes for food. Finally we asked where it was. They said soon. Miraculously it came out moments later. Except they forgot my husband’s food. We asked where it was and the waitress responded that it wasn’t on the tab. My husband said well I definitely ordered it and even repeated it for her.
The is where the 0 star comes in. The waitress responded with a very snarky, and I quote, ‘well I didn’t take your order. What do you want me to do about it?’
She couldn’t have cared less and it was obvious. Which, you know, person to person it’s whatever BUT this was a business and a customer situation… so wildly unprofessional.

REVIEW TEXT I've been coming here off and on for a few years and usually leave with a happy stomache but empty wallet. The cocktails are small, but strong, pricey, and mostly over sweet in my opinion. About $15 for a drink. I love the appetizers however I usually cannot justify the price. I agree with other reviewers that the prices do not reflect what is brought out to you. I find the food to be delicious personally but do think the portions are rather small for the prices.
Now the service here has been poor ever since I can remember. Expect to spend a lot of time waiting and to pay double than what you planned to. I will still go again, just not anytime soon

The service was great, the place was clean, and everyone was incredibly kind and welcoming — serving us with a smile. I’m really glad we chose to come here. It was a great decision!

body.input: REVIEW TEXT We were one of the only tables there. We asked for water no ice and got two waters with ice. I ordered the lobster roll and asked that they omit the salad and I will just get a bowl of chowder and said I understand that would be additional. The waitress said she had to ask the chef who angrily said no loud enough I heard it in the dining room. I just wanted to save them the lettuce but I guess that's not ok? When the lobster roll came out I was SHOCKED. If thats lobster then im Donald Trump. First of all the meat was pigmented pink 100% of the way through not a fleck of white. Also it was preshredded within an inch of its life unlike any lobster roll in the world not a single identifiable piece. The bread was untoasted and tough. It was served on one of those frang outdoor brat buns. My mom ordered a burger that had a SLAB of onion on it. For an $80 meal I am severely disappointed. My view was further validated when I mentioned my meal to a shop next door and they advised they dont eat there either due to the food. Makes sense why it was completely empty for Sunday lunch when the streets are packed.

REVIEW TEXT ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Kelley’s BBQ did NOT disappoint! We ordered the brisket sandwich with cowboy baked beans, potato salad, and a large lemonade — and overall, it was a fantastic meal.

The brisket sandwich was super filling, with meat that was absolutely mouthwatering and melt-in-your-mouth tender. The spicy BBQ sauce complemented it perfectly and added just the right kick without overpowering the flavor.

The cowboy baked beans were a standout — rich, flavorful, and honestly so good I didn’t even want to share!

The potato salad, in my opinion, could use a little improvement. It felt like it was missing a bit of seasoning and salt. It definitely has potential, though — I think adding some bite-sized pickles would really elevate the flavor.

And the lemonade? So refreshing and delicious — the perfect pairing for a BBQ meal.

Overall, I’d absolutely stop by again next time I’m in the area. Great food, generous portions, and a satisfying experience. 10/10 recommend

They even provide blankets if you get a bit chilly. It is worth the wait if happen to come during a busy time.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT My first visit to this restaurant and our menu choices did not measure up to expectations (based upon friends’ recommendations). We ordered lo mein and pork shumai. The shumai were very tough and rubbery to chew and the lo mein was bland, overly oily and strangely pale. Tasted like it had MSG - the sodium content was up there and I love salt. The waitress even mentioned that we should drink a lot of water with our meal! My friend liked the lo mein, but I’ve never had one that lackluster. I went for the comfort food and it didn’t measure up for me. Will return but choose differently. Server was great and the atmosphere was pleasing and not too noisy even though every table was filled when we left. Very popular place- I just need to explore the menu a bit more. Will post another review later.

REVIEW TEXT Had such a wonderful experience at Taste of India! We tried a variety of dishes including the Kadai Paneer, Baingan Bharta, Pakora Platter, Bhel, Paratha, Gajar Halwa, Saffron Ice Cream, and Rasmalai.. and honestly, everything was absolutely delicious.

The Kadai Paneer was rich and flavorful, the Baingan Bharta had that perfect smoky taste, and the Pakora Platter was crispy and fresh. The Bhel was light and tangy, and the parathas were soft and perfectly made. To end on a sweet note, the Gajar Halwa, Saffron Ice Cream, and Rasmalai were all incredible and home made.

What truly made the experience even better was the owner, she was so friendly, welcoming, and genuinely sweet to everyone. You can really feel the warmth and care they put into both the food and the service.

Highly recommend this place if you’re craving authentic and comforting Indian food!

body.input: REVIEW TEXT This is such a cute brunch spot! Something our town was definitely in need of. They decorated in SUCH a cute way and the food was so good! My toddler and I split a Nutella waffle and he definitely loved it. There are a couple of things that I think maybe could be improved that seem to be just because it's a new business and they just haven't started doing those things yet. It was pretty busy when we came and they were having people seat themselves, but the seating is fairly spread out and so people were having to hunt for the one open table kind of thing. I think on busier mornings, seating people instead of free seating might be the move. I would also recommend putting salt and pepper on the tables. Overall we had a great experience. The people were very nice, prices were reasonable and the building was clean. It's kid friendly in that kids can go there, but there were no kids menus or booster seats, so you could bring your kids but it's definitely meant to be a brunch place. There weren't a lot of large tables, so definitely better for a date or a few friends instead of a large group. There is a ramp for accessibility, but it's tight so tables may need to be moved for mobility aids. There is a bar by the toilet and a place to change diapers in the bathroom for those that need it.

REVIEW TEXT What a little gem with new owners! body.input:
REVIEW TEXT ****Please read full review ****Not a good steak house*****honest answer……. 20 oz prime rib 10 oz of pure fat. Filled a bread plate with fat.
The meat was ordered medium rare I received medium rare.
The meat itself was tough poor quality beef I had to saw my knife to cut the meat. I joked to my wife that My arm was tired.
Not tender.
The other steak was over cooked dry and the mushrooms on top burnt…..HEAT LAMP..The garlic Mash potatoes lost their potato flavor because all I could taste was garlic. ( I love garlic) they were not fresh in texture and dry again Heat Lamp …
The iced tea was great.
Waitress was kind but took forever to get iced tea refills.  1 refill in 40 minutes
dinner being served on a (non )busy Friday night was very long too long but not horrible.
Waitress tried way too hard for a tip by asking if I was a bicyclist or athlete and was it normal for me to eat 7,000 calories of meat a day ??? Not sure where that was going.  I would have said yes if she would have said 7,000 calories of fat a day.
The restaurant was clean 12 years of living up the street and nothing has changed  boring atmosphere was like an old folks home with a few intoxicated old guys singing karaoke songs at there table with forks as microphones on a Friday night…I think one farted.
1980s sophisticated steak house  ……the iced tea was good.
But not Don Johnson good!
The lemon in the ice tea was good. But not Rico tubbs good.
The ice was good but not (Miami Vice) good.
As bad as that last reference was so was my $150.00 dinner.
I sincerely just can’t justify why I should return for any reason. …..12 year local. I’ve eaten here at least 1 time every 2 years with same results.

COA restaurant next door is awesome

They are the best. Treat them like it if you go, they deserve every bit of it!

REVIEW TEXT We went to Calico Cupboard for my birthday yesterday with a party of six, and it was such a great experience. The restaurant was a little busy when we arrived, but you would never know it from the service. The staff handled everything with professionalism and warmth.

I ordered the PNW sandwich, and if you haven’t tried it yet, you absolutely should, it’s a 10/10. Perfect flavors and beautifully put together. My daughter had the pulled pork tacos, and she said they were delicious as well. But what really stood out was the service. Our server was wonderful, but even staff who weren’t assigned to our table stopped by to check if we needed refills or anything else. That kind of teamwork and attention is something most restaurants wish they could achieve. Friendly staff, great food, and excellent service made my birthday meal memorable. Highly recommend Calico Cupboard!

REVIEW TEXT Amazing on every level!  You’re greeted by a friendly gentleman that makes you feel like you’re being welcomed into his family home immediately. The service is top notch, specialty board menus that are hand written and explained in decadent detail, which makes it hard to choose just one entree.
The ambiance of this delectable lil restaurant is also authentic to its cuisine and location, set in the quaint little seaside town of Anacortes.
Watching the evening unfold is like a production that has many layers that add to the experience, including a live musician that embellishes the night perfectly.
And the food… I cannot say enough about it all. From the appetizers, salads, entrees, dessert and right down to the lemon drop drink to end it all. Hands down THE BEST Italian food I have ever eaten. Such high quality ingredients that your palette dances to with every bite.
I highly recommend visiting Nonnas , as I know you will not be disappointed at all!

REVIEW TEXT Stopped by La Conner Thai Garden (near Skagit Valley) for lunch and had a pleasant experience overall.

Ambience:
The outdoor seating is the highlight — shaded, surrounded by flowers, and even a small pond nearby. It genuinely feels like a relaxed picnic setting with Thai food. We were seated right away, which was a plus. Street parking is available nearby and easy enough to find.

Food:
I ordered the Massaman curry — flavors were really good and the chicken was well-cooked, but the curry itself felt a bit on the watery side. I ended up finishing the solid portions but left most of the gravy. Still tasty, just could be thicker.
(My wife’s dish was also enjoyable, though I don’t recall the exact name.)

Pricing:

REVIEW TEXT We had a truly memorable experience at Nonna Luisa Ristorante while we were in town for my daughter’s swim meet at the nearby pool — which also happened to fall on her birthday.

From the moment we walked in, the owner welcomed us like family. He is an incredibly kind and gracious gentleman who went out of his way to make my daughter feel special on her birthday. That personal touch meant a lot to us and made the evening unforgettable.

The food was outstanding. Even the seemingly simple Caesar salad tasted different — in the best possible way. You can tell the ingredients are fresh and thoughtfully prepared; the dressing had depth and balance that you don’t often find.

The highlight of the evening was the Lasagna Sofia Loren. It’s a rich, indulgent creation layered with lobster, crab, prawn, and béchamel. The combination is luxurious, creamy, and deeply satisfying without feeling heavy. Every bite felt carefully crafted.

Between the warm hospitality and the exceptional food, this dinner turned a swim meet trip into a beautiful birthday memory. We will absolutely return the next time we’re in the area. Highly recommended.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Rachawadee Thai Cafe is a must-try spot in Mt. Vernon. Other Thai restaurants in the area simply can’t compare. Some of the dishes they serve are even better than what you’ll find in Thailand, yet they manage to maintain authenticity. The restaurant is small but offers a unique dining experience, giving customers a true taste of Thai cuisine "A dish far from home" in an intimate setting.

This is the place for those who’ve found a love for spice. Normally, I need to order level 5 spice at most Thai restaurants to feel satisfied, but here, just 2 or 3 stars pack more than enough heat to thrill my taste buds.

Food Recommendations:

Their Pad Se Ew (stir-fried noodle dish), cooked by the male chef, is one of the few dishes I’ve ever rated a perfect 10/10 in my "food judging" experience. It’s absolutely incredible.

Last week, I had the chance to try their Rad Na, and it’s quickly become my new favorite dish. I've tried this dish at over 50 places in Thailand, but this version stands out as the most exhilarating. The dish packs a powerful kick of spice that elevates it in the most wonderful way. I highly recommend it!

Update: Been coming back to this place, And will keep coming back for the food. 🧡

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Horrible experience today. We were there for over 2 hours total. First waited for 10 or more minutes for waitress to take our order. We ordered a drink and we gave her our food order. Drinks were served promptly. Then the wait for food. Over an hour and a half and no food. She would not swing by the table and explain. I had to track her down twice and ask when we could expect our food. Finally I tracked her down for a third time and she gave the same excuse, they were busy. They were maybe 25% of occupancy. Finally (third time) I found her and said I'd pay for the drinks and we needed to eat elsewhere. She was exasperated (which I had every right to be but wasn't) and frantically tried to find the order on the check spindle. No where to be found. She still took no accountability. I paid and left. I would have at least expected to be comped for the one drink the four of us had. Oh, her parting shot was don't come on a Friday afternoon, we're too busy. I won't come back at all. Problem solved.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT My husband and I were coming here for a simple breakfast date and I thought it was a beautiful place at first. I had ordered a side of eggs with my pancakes and when I went to put some salt on the eggs the salt shaker top came off and salt poured all over the eggs. All I wanted was new eggs and I was perfectly fine with waiting. The salt shaker itself either just fell or a prankster got me so I was in no way or shape mad at them. I waved our server down to just notify her about what had happened and if I could please have new eggs. Sadly though our server came back not even 5 mins later and that was when I realized she just rinsed of the eggs with water cuz they were soaked and I could tell it was the same eggs! I believe it wasn't a big deal to ask for new eggs due to unfortunate events and I sure don't find it appetizing to know that my food was just rinsed off. Do better!

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT This place is an absolute dumpster fire. We waited nearly two hours with no food and no clear timeline, and when we finally told her we were leaving, she still couldn’t give us an answer on when our meal would be ready.

Instead of handling it professionally, she followed us outside and threatened to call the police for theft. That’s completely unacceptable. We had only been served chips and a single horchata, and we left $20 on the table before walking out—far more than what we received.

To be threatened like that after being ignored for hours is beyond frustrating. This wasn’t just bad service—it was handled in a way that felt hostile and completely out of line. Sadly we paid to avoid any dealings with local police in a small town boosted by tourism. I advise go anywhere and everywhere to eat or see tulips.

To make it worse, when the food finally did come out in boxes, the quality and presentation were abysmal—completely underwhelming and nowhere near worth the wait.

If I could give zero stars I would.

REVIEW TEXT We were traveling and staying nearby and decided to give this place a try. Since we’ve visited Ireland before, we thought we’d see if this restaurant had that authentic touch—and wow! Everything was 5 stars.

Our server, Kendall, was next level. He was kind, funny, and attentive, and truly made the experience memorable. We loved it so much that we came back the very next day for lunch.

The food was absolutely delicious. It honestly felt like stepping back in time to when we were in Ireland. The bacon burger was excellent, the turkey dinner was delicious, and the bread pudding was outstanding. We also had the fish & chips, which were fantastic—and they actually give you enough tartar sauce (which we appreciated, lol).

Overall, we highly recommend this place. We only wish we lived in the same state so we could come back more often!

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Was unaware a bakery could get so many things wrong. Croissants super stale despite it being Saturday morning. Actually tough and chewy! Their standard for heating up a pastry is not a convection or toaster oven but a microwave so now it’s tough, chewy, AND gummy.

This is the last time I assume reasonable prices based on blind faith - they don’t bother putting prices on their pastry case. It’s a weirdo pricing breakdown where you see the base croissant price of $4 and then an additional $3 or more for the topping. Almost doubling the price for some slivered almonds and powdered sugar is a bold choice and not one we would have agreed to had we known up front. Just post the prices. This isn’t a lobster restaurant.

If we had known that pastries and coffee would be almost $40 at that quality we would’ve gone elsewhere.

The point of sale transaction was also bizarre because the gal who took our order turned around and started making it, and then somebody else took her place halfway through so we had to go through the order several times.

I don’t understand the 4 1/2 stars for this place and I don’t understand how a place that seems to be pretty well established has such a chaotic front end.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT I was scanning the menu at The Fairhaven while 35 weeks pregnant when my friend said that if I was craving burgers we needed to leave right away and go to Skagit Valley Burger Express. Best decision ever.

Fantastic, tasty, high quality burgers  (fast food costs almost just as much nowadays and is nowhere near the same quality!) that thoroughly satiated my pregnancy craving.

Skagit Western Burger was my favorite and the bleu cheese burger is great too. The fried pickles were too breaded for me but the garlic waffle fries were better than the garlic fries you find at the Mariners games at T-Mobile Stadium. I cannot wait to come back but also thankful I am not a local because I would swing by so often spending all my money on their menu instead of diapers.

They do not have ice! But their mexican coke (glass bottles) and cans of soda are chilled (if you aren't ordering a cold milkshake.)

On a dry, sunny day, the outdoor seating is perfect!! I was pleasantly surprised that they had small bathroom on site. Even though it is small, it is well equipped with soap, hot water, poo pouri, paper towels, and is very clean!

body.input: REVIEW TEXT I passed by this little fish market for several years. Stopped in last year and very rare I pass by without stopping. The lobster roll is great not a big celery person but the little add cruch was good. The crab sandwich is really good also both of the come with plenty of meat. The potato salad that is served with them is fantastisk. Have to get an extra one. The smoked salmon was the start, and let just say I can get 1lb or 5lbs and it gone once the kids find out. And don't let the talk you in to trying the smoked scallops. It's a trick. The crab cakes if you can get them. We'll most crab cakes you dig thru breading to find the crab theirs you dig thru the crab to find the bread. Haven't found anything yet that isn't top rate. Even the customer service. Everybody there are super friendly.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Went here and ordered 2 blizzards and a chicken basket meal. They gave me the wrong blizzard. They made me an oreo instead of a brownie one. So I brought it up. The cashier told the manager because they dont remake them. Then the manager gave me a small plastic container with 5 pieces of brownie in it and walked off,  wanted me to put them in the Oreo shake i didnt order.. So I stayed there and again asked the cashier why there not fixing my order and she tells me my manager wont remake it. I said its not remaking it. I would like to get what I ordered and you guys made the wrong one. Then she goes back to the manager who wont talk to me and tells the cashier to come ask me for my receipt which i tossed out when I grabbed napkins and staws. Told her I literally just paid and got my order. My daughter sitting at the table with the other food. So then they made me stand there for 15 minutes filling other orders ignoring me. Then she finally comes over and throws down a runny chocolate blizzard. 3/4 cup was all syrup and hardy any ice cream. You could tell she purposely sabotaged it. At that point I gave up. Literally tipped it over in the trash and it poured out like water. I didnt get her name she was short Hispanic lady with long black hair  in a pony tail.  Also when we got there. There was a huge line and no one was ringing anyone up. All they were doing was drive through and ignoring the front end. This was my 1st time here and it will be my last. I dont normally write up a review online but felt her attitude was uncalled for. It was simple , they made me the wrong order and was like 30 minutes of arguing to get what I paid for, then got met with attitude . I was polite the whole time. I even apologized although I had no reason to. I wasnt the one who messed up. She has no buisness working there or dealing with customers, I cant believe shes a manager. I feel sorry for those working on her shift.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT We had reservations on a Saturday night for dinner for 4 with steak, seafood, cocktails, appetizers & wine…

Highlights:
-Seared scallops appetizer was delicious. Cooked perfectly.
-Service was really good. It was busy but our waitress was on it.
-Cocktails were delicious. We had the Margarita and a raspberry lemon drop, both great.

Neutral:
-Prices are fair for the product.
-2 in our party thought the steaks were fine.
-Grilled veggies were fine.

Lowlights:
-Bone marrow appetizer tastes good but the portion is minuscule. Not worth the $.
-Too many tables in the dining room. It was very loud and hard to hear.
-2 in our party thought the steaks were bad. My steak was cooked to temp inside but the outside was beyond charred. The only flavor was burnt charcoal which was a bummer. Another in our party had the same issue.
-I know this place is more steak/bourbon than steak/wine but the wine list is pretty sad. Unfortunately Il Granaio (same owners) suffers from the same problem.

Overall, it was an okay experience. The happy hour menu looked decent so maybe I’d go back to try that but I don’t think I would return for another steak if that’s how they cook them all the time.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT In all honesty, this was the worst service I’ve experienced in the Skagit Valley. The younger Asian guy behind the counter seemed like he didn’t even want to be there. The whole experience felt disorganized and frustrating from start to finish.
We ordered our food to dine in and were already behind a family of 3 in line. Those customers were served within about 10 minutes. Meanwhile, three more people ordered after us and still got their food before we did. We ended up waiting around 45 minutes before our food finally came out.
While we were waiting, we watched several customers get their meals, eat a little, and then throw most of their food away. After finally getting ours, I understand why.
For the price, the food is extremely overpriced for the value. They advertise Angus beef, but it tasted very cheap and had an unpleasant flavor. I’ve had Angus burgers from many other places nearby and they don’t taste anything like that.
Our meal came out to about $30 per person, which is crazy considering the portion sizes. Their “large” feels more like a small. The burger itself was about the size of a Double Jumbo Jack, except you’re paying almost double the price compared to a $16 meal at Jack in the Box with fries and a drink.
When the food finally came out, the employee approached us like he wasn’t even sure the meal was ours, which just added to the awkward experience.
The only decent thing were the onion rings, but even those were almost $10 for a very small portion, which again feels overpriced.
Overall, the service was poor, the wait time was ridiculous, and the value just isn’t there. I honestly felt like I got scammed, and I’ll gladly take my business somewhere else next time where the service and quality match the price.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT We came here to celebrate my son’s birthday, and it ended up being one of those meals where everything just hit.

My husband and I had the Steakhouse Burger - a double smash patty with American cheese, bourbon-glazed onions, mayo, and house-made steak sauce on a kaiser roll, served with garlic parmesan fries. The onions were unreal, and the fries were spot on, perfectly crisp with just the right amount of seasoning.

My son ordered the 8 oz. Wagyu Zabuton steak with bourbon compound butter, and it was so tender he could cut it with a spoon. His sides were asparagus and wild rice pilaf. My other son had the tomahawk pork chops with roasted sweet potatoes and broccolini. It was apparently amazing because his plate disappeared before I could even get a photo. My daughter-in-law went with the New York strip with Truffle potatoes au gratin and lemon truffle asparagus. She said it was excellent as well.

I also added a Caesar salad with my burger. The house-made croutons, candied bacon, and pecorino really elevated it, and the dressing was fantastic.

Drinks were just as good. Cocktails and Glenlivet all around, no complaints there. We thought about dessert, but the portions are generous and we were completely full.

The staff were all friendly and attentive without being intrusive.

Parking can be a bit of a challenge, but that’s just the reality of that part of downtown Mount Vernon and not the restaurant’s fault.

Overall, it was a great night. It’s not cheap, but the quality matches the price. Definitely worth it for a special occasion. As I said, we were celebrating my son’s birthday and it felt like the perfect place for it. Highly recommend.

REVIEW TEXT I came in for dinner and left questioning whether I had just been served by a human or some kind of hospitality wizard sent from another dimension. Demitri didn’t just take our order—he curated an experience. I’m pretty sure he could sense when my drink was getting low before I even knew it myself. At one point I blinked and—boom—refill. Either incredible service or mild psychic abilities.

His timing? Impeccable. His humor Top-tier. Demitri’s ability to make us feel like the most important table in the room.  Honestly suspicious.

If this server ever leaves, I will have no choice but to follow him to whatever restaurant is lucky enough to get him  next. Five stars isn’t enough. I’m prepared to start a petition for six.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT We ordered three items. Pad Thai with Beef, Panang Curry with Chicken & Fried Rice with Pork. Starting with the Pad Thai, the noodles were thinner than I was expecting but still very appetizing. The flavor was exactly as you’d expect. The meat was tender and juicy. However, since the noodles are so thin, heating them up later to eat as leftovers led to a very strange unappetizing texture so just make sure you eat em up right away. As for the Panang Curry, this is actually my favorite food, so I was most excited for this. That being said, I’m not quite picky with it as it can be so versatile however the amount of fish oil used was so off putting I couldn’t bring myself to take more than a few bites. I’m unsure if the oil was to blame but the entire curry was VERY runny as well. Like water over the plate. Lastly the rice. I had such high hopes for the rice. It looked absolutely scrumptious. However it was so bland. If not for the pork and peas, there’d be no flavor at all.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT i hate leaving negative reviews, but this is now my second bad experience with this coffee stand. i come by often since it’s on my route to work, but i will no longer give them my money. i spent 12 mins in line behind the car at the window, i figured they had a lot of drinks and tried to give some grace, but then after they got their drinks the baristas were just talking to them. the customer handed them gifts and they left- after 2 mins of talking. i understand having regulars as someone who’s worked in coffee and service industry and wanting to chat, but holding up a long line is not good practice. when i got to the window there was no conversation with me whatsoever, i ordered a large redbull and a breakfast sandwich & my sandwich was missing the cream cheese that they asked me if i wanted and charged me for. when i asked the girl to break a bill for me so that i could tip - my total was exactly 20, she handed me a 10 and 2 5s. i don’t like not tipping so i handed them a 5 but i just want management to know that your girls dropped the ball this morning and did not deserve a tip at all. do better. the first time i came and had a bad experience there was giant floaters in my drink, i asked them to remake it and they handed the same one back. horrible stand don’t give them your money.

Mac & Cheese was bland and the coleslaw was just mayonnaise taste, baked beans was watery and flavorless plus cornbread was dry which was the sweet bread.  I also got a burger for my dad’s birthday and mom had the sliders and my parents said it was eh but the fries was good. The best thing tonight was the Dr Pepper and bbq sauce, for 120 bucks I wanted it to be better then it was.  Service is always great and the customers are awesome and very kid friendly place.  Would love to talk to the owners or the new owner of this establishment.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT I have to give a huge shoutout to everyone at Double Barrel. We've used them a couple times for catering where I work and they've been just the best to work with and the food is always amazing. But today they went above and beyond. We had a little mishap with our lunch timing and accidentally put a 45 person catering order in for about 3 hours later than we needed it. We called in a panic as soon as we realized what happened and the kitchen manager and everyone else there was able to rearrange and get us lunch about an hour and a half earlier than we ordered it for. I don't know what kind of magic they worked but it was just as good as it always is. I know my day was chaotic and I can only imagine how their day went because they went out of their way to help us out with our mistake. We will most definitely be using Double Barrel again.... that is, if they'll have us back!

REVIEW TEXT My date the other night and I went in there.
●  Service
Up at the front counter was brand new kis hosting alone first night, maybe his first hour. My date spoke Spanish, the kid behind the counter did not.  So okay he's learning.
●   Food
The food was horrible, my date said "there's probably a reason they sell so much tequila".
● Atmosphere
It was pretty unprofessional to leave the new host up front by himself without knowing the menu nor the register although he handled it quite well I would say.
~   side bar.  ~
I'm not sure about you, but when I go to Mexican restaurant, and I ask about something off off the menu, and one of the employees has no idea what it is or how to even spell it let alone pronounce it?  You have a management problem.
Not to mention when we also added in order to go, When we arrived to our destination with the food there was 0 silverware 0 napkins and the food was less than par and light weight. My date was really bummed out cause he was excited to take everybody to any restaurant. I told him to go back and say something but he's too nice to be a guy so hopefully you guys have a better experience than you did. Good luck and thank you host boy for pulling through on your own kid!!!

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Such amazing food. I spent a few months in India and have been trying to find comparable eats ever since and I’ve found that with Curry Leaf. This is food packed full of flavor and made with love. It’s a home cooked meal with farm fresh ingredients. Sooooo so good! Shyni, the chef/owner/farmer is so welcoming, generous and kind! I love that she has a living menu that changes with what’s in season. She is such a gem and this is such a great addition to Anacortes! I’d drive long distances for her food and feel blessed to have it right here! Thank you Shyni! You and your friendly staff are amazing and we’ll definitely be back.

Parking was hard to find, it is tulip time, but it was worth the search.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Wow this place was so good I had to come write a review. We randomly stopped on the way back to Seattle from Anacortes looking for some caffeine and a snack, but when I looked at the menu I started to get excited. We ordered the cinnamon toasties, spicy pork sandwich, kbbq bun, and a matcha latte and Americano. Everything was so good. Cinnamon toasties tasted like a piece of heaven. The spicy pork was delicious and the bread it was on was perfect to balance out the sandwich. Kbbq bun was also great. Everything was very affordably priced especially for the quality and sizes plus the service was amazing. The cashier informed me they don’t accept tips which makes me believe they actually pay their staff fairly. This made me appreciate the great service even more because I realized it was far better than what I feel obligated to tip 20% for at other restaurants. They also have games to play while you eat, a nice environment inside, and even gave us a free brownie when they realized they overcharged for a flavored sweetener in the matcha. Can’t recommend a stop here enough.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT We have been so excited for Curry Leaf to open and bring Indian food to Anacortes. It was everything we hoped it would be! It’s on Commercial next door to the Brown Lantern. It’s a fun, intimate setting. Delicious food with very savory tastes and mild/moderate spice levels. The owner was there and explained that the menu will change every week so each trip will be an adventure. The meal came as a combo plate that served two and included a dessert. Portions were plenty to fill both of us up. This week chicken thali was on the menu and that’s what’s pictured here. There were several small dishes and various sauces that we could mix and match. All of them were delicious, unique and authentic - every one of them was new to us.  So excited to see what else she cooks up! We will definitely be back

body.input: REVIEW TEXT The other day we went out for dinner to celebrate my son’s birthday at our favorite Mexican restaurant. When we were seated, we had told the waiter we were out celebrating my son’s birthday. She wished him happy birthday and said they’d have something for him at the end. Meanwhile while we were there another table had a birthday and they brought out dessert, sang to the table and even had a candle/sparkler placed on the dessert (which is very typical as we have celebrated birthdays there in the past). As we were wrapping up our dinner, the waiter for our table switched with someone else and another lady took over. She didn’t mention anything about the birthday desert and asked for payment. I asked again if we could do something and she said that she’d “try to get something but they’re slammed back there and either way it’ll take some time to cook the desert.” We didn’t mind waiting to celebrate so we told her that was okay, we are super excited to surprise our son. Once the dessert was ready, she brought a very underwhelming dessert compared to the other table that was celebrating, there was no sparkler/or candle and they didn’t sing to my son. I was extremely disappointed especially being a regular and seeing others getting better treatment. I used to really love this place by this service left a bad taste.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT My mom and I visited and we always struggle with finding her food she can eat with celiacs. Their menu for it is limited but the employee/owner was super helpful. We always struggle with things being cross contaminated and understand if it happens on accident a lot. She ordered an asian pear salad with a side of chicken she said was really good. Initially she thought it came with  fried wontons that weren't gluten free due to being fried, and the employee realized she had picked it off and separated it. He came over and explained it wasn't fried in a frier that also cooks with gluten. I thought that was really nice of him because when it comes to food restrictions we're constantly doing double takes due to how often she gets a soup with crackers that come to find out aren't gluten free and she is horribly sick for a few days.

Now to people who don't have dietary restrictions. I got a pork belly sandwich that was so delicious. I have a low low white people spice tolerance so it did have a spice to it, but the flavors were so so good. I'm not usually a soft meat enjoyer, but the pork belly was juicy and had so much flavor when combined with everything else. It genuinely might be my favorite sandwich I've had in a long time. I look forward to trying out their cafe and other food. The fries are also gluten free but I ordered them with my sandwich and they're reminiscent of the five guys fries my dad loves, but I think they're a better fry. I had the house sauce and that was a good dip for fries and pouring on the sandwich but not as special. The real treat is that sandwich. I couldn't finish it all so I ended up with leftovers that were gone that evening before I was even supposed to have dinner.

Edit: I found their Instagram and it looks like there are more gluten free options than we thought. Definitely will be bringing my mom back to try. My only wish is that they maybe had a handheld menu with ingredients listed so we could see what is/isn't gluten free a little easier but being a small business this is understandable. I think from other reviews the owner is the one we talked to, and he was super nice and super helpful with answering all our questions and hesitancy. Highly recommend.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT I'd heard good things about this place and decided to check it out. Ordered the Kbbq Beef sandwich, spicy pork fries, a cinnamon roll, and the lemon cheesecake cookie. The beef sandwich was delicious- super flavorful, excellent bread, and a good amount of meat for a $13 sandwich. I'd probably ask for extra veggies next time, but all in all, great. The fries were really well done, also. Again, super flavorful. Crispy fries underneath a good amount of spicy pork with a tasty gochujang aioli on top, and only $8! Ordered ketchup on the side- tasted homemade and was delish. The pastries I was a little less impressed. The cinnamon roll was slightly tough and not quite enough frosting, IMO. But the flavor was really good. The lemon cheesecake cookie was a good cookie base, and the lemon curd was also yummy, but the cheesecake part was very small compared to the rest of the cookie. When I got to that part, it was amazing though. The staff was friendly; it seemed like they were training someone new on the register but everyone was friendly and helpful, and the service was fast. All in all, an excellent addition to the MV food scene!

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Very disappointing.  We have had great meals here in the past, but at our most recent visit, the food was not well executed and the service was poor.  They do a good job of sourcing local ingredients, but the problem is in the execution.  Our mains were served cold and my husband's salmon was overcooked.  The portions were small, which would be ok had they been better executed and/or at not such a high price point.  They also seem to have a problem with stocking liquor/wine.  We were told there was told there was no "cocktail menu" and were served the house old fashioneds, which were much too sweet.  They also did not have many of the wines listed on their wine list, with the only ones remaining in the $100 range.   Sadly, it ended up being a very expensive and very mediocre meal.

REVIEW TEXT My elderly mom and I had been here before. She and I liked the food and service this past August so we planned our trip to enjoy dinner here again while I was working in town. We walked into sit down at 7:10p and the man behind the counter punched the wall behind the counter in a violent rage as another customer walked away from the counter with a take out order. He continued his rant by  punching supply boxes and yelling while a woman from the kitchen was also yelling loudly at him. My Mom and I were stunned and scared to death from the abrupt noise, yelling in anger and escalation of the situation so quickly. The man turned around looked at us and said, “we are closed, we are not serving anyone else!” and did a swiping motion with his hands in front of his body. My Mom and I quickly turned around and left, still shocked by what had just occurred.

I have been in customer service for 30 years and have never been fearful in an establishment, nor had an employee that displayed that much rage during a situation, this was a first.  This is the second review in 4 mo of the front counter man being rude.  If I were you considering to eat here, with so many other choices in Anacortes, I would not support this business. (The system made me provide a rating thus the 1 star but in general I would not have provided a positive on any scale).

REVIEW TEXT Edit ..again this time I went my breakfast was not good. Burnt pieces of hash browns.. the gravy tasted old and cold my wife's bacon was obviously over cooked and deep-fried. I used to be a breakfast cook and with no one in the restaurant this shouldn't be an issue. I dont think ill go back. And it was the better part of 100 bucks...

Then our order came out and looked good enough, but as I cut into the eggs, I realized they were still raw, and the whites were still clear and stringy at this point my patients is gone and I'm feeling like my meal was a bust and for 47$( with tip) for 2 breakfasts I would be hesitant to try it again. After all that, I might have comped the coffee or something, but no such luck. I hate giving a bad review, but this was our experience, and it wasn't great.

REVIEW TEXT After eating at Calico Cupboard, I felt safe and excited to find out there was also a location in Anacortes. Unfortunately, the experience there was very different.

When we arrived, we waited a full 10 minutes in the small entry area before even being acknowledged. There was no one else waiting, and there were at least two open tables. Despite that, no one made eye contact or greeted us. Eventually, an employee called out that someone would be with us “soon,” but that turned into another 5 minutes while tables were reset—leaving us just standing there.

When we were finally seated, the employee gruffly explained that they only had one server and that’s why we had to wait. It didn’t come across as apologetic—more like she was irritated that we had come in at all.

To be fair, our server herself was fine. She brought drinks and gave us time with the menu. And the food? Delicious—absolutely worth the trip in that sense.

But if you’re looking for a welcoming experience and good ambiance, I would recommend the Mount Vernon location instead. If you don’t mind a less friendly atmosphere, the food at the Anacortes location is still very good.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT I recently tried Good To Go Grill and had a really great experience overall!

The service was warm and personal — a sweet older lady helped me at the counter, and although I didn’t see who was cooking in the back, everything felt very homemade and cared for. She told me my order would take about 10 minutes, so I waited in my car… and sure enough, in about 8 minutes she came out and knocked on my window to hand me my food. That alone was such a nice touch!

I ordered the orange chicken with sticky rice, plus a matcha boba with lychee tea. The boba drink was a little sweeter than I usually like, but wow — it was still SO good.

Now the food — the portion size was HUGE. I honestly wish I had taken a picture before I started eating because I barely made a dent and still had more than half left. Definitely great value for the price.

The orange chicken was really tasty with nicely breaded chicken. I personally would’ve loved just a little more sauce, but I did notice on the menu you can order extra sauce, so that’s on me for next time. The sticky rice was absolutely delicious, and I really appreciated that they gave a small cup of thick soy sauce instead of those annoying little packets — such a simple but thoughtful upgrade.

The salad was good too — fresh and solid for a side.

Overall, everything tasted fresh and made to order, and you can tell they take pride in what they serve.

9/10 — I’ll definitely be back!

REVIEW TEXT Calico Cupboard is one of those places that you NEED to go to when you're in town.

When you get there, you just sign in yourself at the stand which is a good system so no one has to check you in when they're already pretty busy. While you're waiting you can go to the shop down the stairs or go to the dessert area right next to the waiting area to get some great desserts. Last time i was there I saw frosted cream cheese sugar cookies, and pies, and more.

When you get seated there are so many great food options, lots of options, same with drinks.

They are only open until 3:30 pm so be sure to manage time well. And don’t expect an empty place, it's usually populated. Tight space, so scoot in those chairs as far as you can.

Staff were laid back, and nice. When they’re busy make sure to be patient with the staff, they’re dealing with tons of other orders as well.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT My husband made early, around 5:00 reservations for a Saturday for us. We got seated very quickly. The hostess and waitress were very friendly. The restaurant looks so cute and unique. We order the 4-course special. I asked for gluten free pasta. The waitress offered me Insalata Caprese in place of the bruschetta.  It was great and I appreciated her offering. The house salads were very underwhelming, dish of iceberg lettuce a piece of cucumber, and a piece of tomato. I asked for Italian vinaigrette and it was thick like Kraft dressing. Some might like this but the salads I make at home are much more healthy and interesting. We waited a very long time for our main courses to come. Our wooden chairs were becoming very uncomfortable by this time. Our waitress apologized for the delay and asked if we wanted anything while we waited. We declined. I ordered the Pollo Clabrese Pasta as my main. I loved it and I was not disappointed at all with the GF pasta. When we were ready select our dessert options, we ask to be reminded of the dessert options, assuming she would tell us what was included with the 4-course special. My husband enjoyed his tiramisu but was surprised by the upcharge when the bill came. The Panna Cotta without the raspberry sauce (to make it GF), or the spumoni was recommended for me.  I went for the Panna Cotta as I'd never tried it. This was a very bland choice for a dessert. Two hours after sitting down. We were finally complete and very sore. The soft chairs of our car were a relief.  Overall, a mediocre experience.

REVIEW TEXT The space is welcoming and clean. The staff were so friendly and engaging. The food was amazing! I could have filled up on the gyozas, in fact I may choose them as my entree another time. I had the prawn ramen. There were 4 or 5 large prawns in the bowl along with chunks of mushroom and other gems. The broth was so good that I ate it well past the point when I was full! Next time I just won’t eat all of the filling noodles.
It is obvious that this place is loving managed and run by a family. My only suggestion is that they could use a more visible sign to alert people that it is there. Don’t miss it!

REVIEW TEXT Ribeye Medium - cooked perfect.. but it needed more seasoning. It felt like I was adding salt after every other bite.

Loaded baked potato - really good. They put the toppings on the side and not on the potato.  Which I thought was weird, but I feel like I got more toppings that way, so it wasn't a problem.

Pan Fried Oysters - They were good and were pretty big in size..

Hefeweizen Beer - It was good.

Service - My waitress was Joy. She was very nice and friendly.  She came around pretty often to make sure I was ok. She was very upbeat and happy. I would love to have her as my waitress again.

Bill - Somewhere around $75 Total was about $100 after a 25% tip.

REVIEW TEXT I heard a customer ahead of me say this was the best restaurant in town. I was not disappointed. Since I’m a gluten free celiac I was in awe to find everything on the menu possible for me. I chose the falafel wrap which was amazing.  It was stuffed with falafel, roasted onions, red peppers, sprouts, greens, hummus, avocados, and vegan ranch dressing.  I wouldn’t have called it a wrap because it was a warm flatbread on the outside which made this a huge meal.
The vibe in the restaurant was relaxed and the servers were helpful. Lots of tasty treats available too. My wife had the walnut taco salad and loved it.
Put this on your list while visiting Anacortes even if you are not vegan or gluten free. So good!!

body.input: REVIEW TEXT I am from out of town and stopped here before going to the tulip festival! The staff was so incredibly nice and helpful when it came to recommendations for food! I don't drink coffee but the breakfast and pastry options were incredible! I ended up getting one of the breakfast burritos which the put in the panini press! It makes it so much less messy when eating and has a nice crisp on the outside! I also bought a pastry which had berries and lemon cream on top. Truly delicious! I also love the local artists paintings on the wall for purchase! I would 100% recommend coming here!

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Granaio Italian Restaurant was the perfect venue for the April '26 monthly meeting for our Car Club! We reserved the restaurant for 2 hours on the weekend during the Tulip festival. Our servers Stephanie and Elizabeth were so helpful, they made the whole experience so stress-free!

We got to the restaurant an hour early to setup the Auxiliary meeting room we reserved for our club meeting. After talking with the servers, it was decided that it may not be big enough for a group of our size. The servers graciously offered to close off the main portion of the restaurant instead, and redirect the normal patrons to the Auxiliary meeting room. This worked excellent, and there was plenty of space for our club to meet!

The servers also helped up re-arrange the tables to suit our needs, and we had plenty of space. The menus worked great, and the food was absolutely delicious. Additionally, we had one or two guests who had dietary restrictions, and the servers were more than accommodating to them.

Our club meeting also went very well! The restaurant was quiet and we had no trouble hearing our president and officers make announcements. The servers very discreetly gathered up the checks, and nobody had any complaints about things not being processed properly. Overall, the officers commented about how accommodating the restaurant was and how the servers went out of their way to make our meeting work well. And it did - we one of the highest turnouts of any non-holiday meeting despite the rain. Thanks so much for the great experience. We will be back next year!

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT - great food, but they overcharged us -

We got here the first thing in the morning at 10:30 am, but the parking lot was completely full. We had to camp for a spot for a bit until someone left. The parking lot outside the restaurant was a free public parking lot, and it was quite difficult to find a spot with the fair going on. There were several parties before us, but I believe they just opened up the second floor for seating. We waited longer to get a parking spot tbh. I'd recommend putting your name down on the wait-list when you are waiting for a parking spot to save some time. The restaurant was connected to a cute shop and it was fun to walk around it while waiting too.

Our wait at the restaurant was only about 10-15 minutes. We sat upstairs at a table for 4 with a high chair for my daughter. We ordered the morning glory omelette and the lunch special (soup with turkey sandwich?), a hot latte, and a huge cream puff to go. I made food to feed my daughter, but she wasn't super cooperative so it was a bit messy on the floor when we left (ting food scraps). I believe my husband tipped more for that.

The food was great.. the sandwich had artichokes in there and it was delicious. My husband didn't really care for it, but I thought it was cooked perfectly. The chowder had tons of stuff in there, so it was quite filling. It was definitely not much soup but mostly potato, clams, and other stuff. The omelette was good, but the highlight was actually the jam that comes with the toast. The waiter, Nicolas, told us that everything was made fresh in the house. We wanted to buy the jam afterwards, but didn't see it on sale downstairs.

The bathroom upstairs are singles, so you might want to go downstairs to avoid waiting too long since there was even a line for the man's restroom for a bit too, which is a rare sight.

My husband paid for the food when I was changing my daughter's diaper, so I didn't realize the restaurant overcharged us for two things that we didn't order. You could tell it's someone else's order as it's on top and Nicolas probably made a mistake. It was quite upsetting, but the way back home was nearly 2 hours and it wasn't worth a stop at the restaurant to fix this.

I was told that they use a machine for the bill so you can't see what you ordered or anything. I think the restaurant should definitely be more careful about this and I'm not sure how frequently this happens because you won't even know if you don't check the receipt in the email. I've attached for proof and just be more careful about overcharge from this restaurant. It's a shame because I enjoyed the food and everything, so that totally ruined it for me as that has never happened to me anywhere else.

REVIEW TEXT Disappointing "Authentic" Experience – Misrepresented Dish and Dismissive Service

I’ve had Stir-Fried Basil with Prawn (Pad Krapow) in authentic restaurants from Thailand to Alaska, and it is usually one of my favorite dishes. Unfortunately, what was served here was a massive disappointment.
A proper Basil Prawn dish should highlight the prawns, fresh basil, and chili. Instead, this plate was filler-heavy, packed with cabbage, broccoli, carrots, and onions, with almost no prawns or basil in sight. It felt more like a generic vegetable stir-fry than the specific Thai classic I ordered.
We also ordered the Tom Yum Seafood Rice, which was also far from the authentic Thai flavors we expected.
The most upsetting part, however, was the service. When the staff asked for our feedback, we tried to politely explain that this version was very different from the authentic dish we’ve enjoyed elsewhere. Instead of listening, the staff member shut us down immediately, claiming they are "authentic" and essentially told us we didn't know what we were talking about.
If you are looking for the true flavors of Thailand, I’d suggest skipping this place. To the management: I highly recommend watching any of the hundreds of authentic recipes available online to see how this dish is actually prepared. We came in craving a favorite meal and left frustrated and unheard.

REVIEW TEXT Location: It's between Mount Hood and Anacortes and there has always been great seating everything we have gone (three times as I am writing this).  If you are going to the tulip festival then it is a short drive from the tulip route.

Food: Many of the menu items are fantastic, I've had their basic burger, upgraded Mac and Cheese, and fish and chips.  My wife really liked the chicken pot pie.  However we did find it weird that they really focus on traditional Irish food and yet the fish and chips is just as good as anywhere else in the states, and they have things like Irish nachos and Irish poutine (have not tried them), but tye Irish soda bread was good.  In Ireland they freely give out soda bread, but ours was $5.

Atmosphere:  Big open space with alot of wood largely perimeter seating, but despite being in such a big space still felt cramped to optimize seating.  Last time we went they had live music which really complimented the atmosphere.

Service:  Staff was quite friendly and very responsive to our needs.  Twice we have ordered an appetizer and it was forgotten and instead brought with the meal, but otherwise no complaints.

REVIEW TEXT We’ve been coming here for years because the food is fantastic and the ambiance is great. Unfortunately, none of that matters anymore because the service—specifically from a server named Clayton—has become unacceptable.

This wasn’t a one‑time issue. Clayton has been subpar on multiple visits, but this last experience was the final straw. He dropped off our food and then completely disappeared. My husband’s order was wrong, but since no one ever checked on us, he just ate it. I sat with an empty drink for nearly half an hour.

When we finally asked for a manager, we were told there wasn’t one. Ten minutes later, a woman showed up and acted annoyed that we even asked. That level of dismissiveness tells me the problem goes beyond one server.

It’s incredibly disappointing to say this, but we won’t be returning. Great food can’t make up for consistently bad service and zero accountability.

REVIEW TEXT Where to begin..
Walking in, the old Shari’s building is definitely updated… like Seattle/Bellevue updated 😬. We were sat in the back on the left side… host spoke really quiet so all I caught was scan and menu so I just pieced the rest together. Server seemed stressed but was nice.. “buffet” was on the right side so we had to walk past the host station where customers were standing to pay or be seated.. not ideal with hands full of plates and sauce but oh well. We ordered as much as possible because after reading the reviews we knew we would have to wait 15 minutes before ordering again. one thing I ordered was the avocado salad.. no sauce no dressing… my husband let me know there’s sauces and dressing at the “buffet” station.. no.. just dipping sauces and Mayo .. the salad was spring mix and avocado.. not much flavor there without a dressing or sauce so I went with tempura sauce.. it tasted better I guess. I think the best thing I had was the shrimp ramen but the ratios are off.. It has two tempura shrimp half egg and two bites of noodles. But those two bites of noodles were yummy, still hungry though.. the deep fried roll was stale (like it was fried in advance and sauce put on later) my tuna avocado roll was nothing short of pathetic.. I’m not sure of what my husband thought of his rolls and I know our daughter liked their chicken wings at the “buffet”. We  didn’t like the miso?, tasted like they put too much miso paste in it.
The more people that entered the place the louder the music got.. the group of guys we were sat near didn’t care that children were around while loudly dropping F bombs..
Yes yes yes it’s a soft open but soft opens are what could make or break new businesses in this area. My experience could detour friends/family or maybe a reader from not wanting to eat here or they could just say I’m picky (which yes sometimes I can be..) but I guess try it for yourself and see if it’s worth the price/experience.

Oh yeah that robot thing is AWKWARRDDDDD.. it brings your sushi and just stays there and then finally after 30 seconds leaves. Like imagine a server just standing there after serving you.. just… standing…. there… yeah I know I’m being ridiculous it’s a dang robot but ahh awkward!! Hahaha

REVIEW TEXT I ordered from the taco truck in Anacortes last night through their online system. Both of our orders were accepted, cards were charged, and I was given a pickup time.

When I arrived at the location… the truck was gone.

I called and their recording said they were open until 8 PM (it was around 6 PM). I called their Burlington location to figure out what was going on. The employee told me, very casually, “yeah, they closed early,” as if, duh, I should have known. As if that was a sufficient answer to the problem. No apology, no attempt to fix it.

I asked why their system would still accept orders and charge customers if they had already closed. I was simply told the manager would call me the next day.

No one called.

I followed up the next afternoon, and again was told the manager wasn’t there and would call me “tomorrow.” When I explained I had already been told that, I was met with “it’s not my fault” and no effort to resolve the issue. Again, no apology.

At this point, I’ve been charged for food I never received, driven out of my way for nothing, and gotten zero communication or accountability.

I understand that sometimes places have to close early, but my interaction with the employee and how casual she was about it makes me feel like this is more common than an occasional issue or emergency. Either way, continuing to take orders and charge people is unacceptable, especially when there is no communication, no follow-up, and no effort to make it right. This shows a complete lack of accountability to customers.

The situation was frustrating. But the lack of accountability and zero attempt to fix it kind of blows my mind.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT I stumbled across this gem after visiting the Skagit Valley Tulip Festival. It was a Saturday evening, and the place was fairly busy. I saw it had good reviews online, but mostly I was starving and needed to eat asap. Man, that worked out for me.

The meal I ate was one of my favorite meals I’ve ever eaten. The African-spiced cauliflower will live rent-free in my head for years to come. It was perfectly spiced, warm, not exactly hot, and the cauliflower maintained its texture though deep fried. That’s a feat in and of itself. I had my eye on the carrot appetizer as well, but alas, I am a one-woman show.
The dinner special was a delicious looking halibut and orzo dish. My server, John C, filled me in that the sushi is served on a limited menu and is really a treat. I ordered the chef’s special roll, and I think my personal bar for sushi is forever raised. It was arguably a perfect roll, the ratios were divine.

I then asked John if I could have all my menus back because I wasn’t ready to end this experience yet. He filled me in on the dessert menu, and my ears perked up on the blueberry cake, the crème brûlée, and the lovely lemon dessert. The lovely lemon was a lemon sugar cookie type of base, lemon cream, lemon whip? Lemon lemon lemon. Sounded like a citrus paradise to me. I ate half, and saved the rest for my midnight snack.

TLDR? Service was excellent, food was incredible, ambience was cool and unassuming. Everyone was down to earth and helpful, really leaning into the all-hands-on-deck type of team you need in a full scale restaurant. I can’t wait to come back.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT If you're a person who appreciates a higher level of quality in your food when dining, this place is a gem. We could immediately tell that the chef / kitchen staff are passionate about offering artistically presented dishes that are meticulously designed and very tasty.

Drinks - My wife and I ordered one Old-Fashioned each and the drinks were made pretty close to perfectly, as you might expect if you were at a high-end steakhouse. Because of this, we had to order one more after.

Food - We started with escargot. As people who have French Chefs in our family, we are pretty picky on how escargot is done. This escargot was excellent. It came with perfectly toasted bread and had lots of flavor.
Next, we had mussels. Again, they were done right. Another 10/10. Our waiter offered us more bread at no cost so that we could enjoy the delicious broth that the mussels were in with it.

For our main course, we had the filet mignon (cooked and seasoned pretty close to perfectly) and the fish dish on an encrusted rice cake-like food. Of all the different items we had, this was the only item that was lost on me. It was presented beautifully and artistically, but (this may just be a personal taste thing) the flavor and texture was not to my liking. Please do not let this dissuade you though. Even in the dish that wasn't my personal taste, I could see the care and attention to detail and quality that the chef had put into the dish.

I can't help but give this place 5 stars and now I have an amazing restaurant to go to whenever I visit La Conner. I can't wait to see what other treasures this chef has come up with!

Service - Moe was our server. Immediately we could tell that even though he was serving us, he is definitely a great chef as well and I'd love to try his food sometime as well. He offered great service as did every other staff member we spoke to while there.

Price - For the level of quality they offer, we had absolutely no problem with their prices. Their prices are fair. I think anyone would be hard pressed to find a restaurant offering that level of quality at a lower price.

Thanks for the great experience, Moe and team. We will be back!

Mark.

REVIEW TEXT We were on vacation, and because my husband's name is Connor, we had to come explore La Conner! We were hungry for lunch after the tulip festival, so we drove up here. There is some street parking, but we ended up parking in a public parking lot north of the cafe.
The place is cute and charming, and it's decorated with art that is for sale. The menu on the wall was just for drinks, and their food menu was laminated nearby for us to peruse. We had a nice chat with JJ (who I think is the co-owner), and he was very bubbly and nice. It was fun to witness his kindness to other customers and neighbors as they came in. This place seems very involved with the community.
There are a few tables both outside and inside. The TV behind us was playing Pandora for radio music. Nearby, they had some free chocolate-covered coffee beans and your own water and silverware station.
I got an Arnold Palmer, and boy, was it tart! I got my own sugar to try to sweeten it up.
I also ate the Ricky Ricardo panini, and it wasn't my favorite. The aioli wasn't flavorful enough for me to notice, or maybe it was missing, and the pickles were too thick. I didn't love the flavor profile on this sandwich, and it was pretty hot (in temperature) to eat, so I had to let it cool down a bit.
Connor loved his smoked salmon toast! There were a ton of capers, so lots of salt there. The herbed cream cheese was the star of the show, with the flavorful toast being a close second. He really appreciated it.
I think I'd be happy to come back and try a different sandwich.

REVIEW TEXT What a total letdown! My family and I were on our way back from Canada and we had a sudden craving for bagels so we stopped by this place. Well, given the 4+ reviews we saw in Google Maps, we took a detour to this place. Totally opposite of what we were expecting. The service was slow( took 20+
mins for our orders to arrive) the place is a dump ( supposed to be edgy I guess with the bagel flour bags covering the walls), the floor was littered with crumbs and there was no place to sit. The coffee bar ( which is like a partitioned bar with Torani syrups) and plastic cups was already closed when we got there at 1:45. There were 7 people at the back supposed to be doing the food prep, but I can see only 2 of them actually doing the work. The rest proceeded to mill about, walk slowly around and “supervise”. They don’t seem to be in a hurry to provide service. Highly dissatisfied and tremendously disappointed. Will not recommend.

REVIEW TEXT Favorite bagels in the Seattle area!! Coming from the East Coast, I’ve had the privilege of having constant access to great bagels for so long that I forgot how _impossible_ it is to find one on the other coast. However, Whidbey Island Bagels brings the NYC bagel across the country, with a perfectly soft and pillowy interior and delightful crust.

I love the wide variety of flavors, but they definitely sell out; come early if you’re hoping for one of their more popular flavors. I, personally, love the rosemary sea salt — it has just the right amount of savoriness and flavor without overpowering the rest of the bagel. I just got it with plain cream cheese, but they have plenty of fun flavors of cream cheese, hummus, peanut butter, and egg sandwich toppings.

This place is always bustling, so I’d expect a pretty long line and decent wait. However, the service is as efficient and friendly as can be, and it’s 100% worth the wait and 1-hour drive out of Seattle.

Note: The bagels also freeze extremely well, so you can always take a couple dozen home to make the trek more worthwhile :)
